description: A C# game engine in which a program opens a window, draws each frame with plain static calls named as raylib's functions are, and draws Dear ImGui in the same frame, over SDL3, Vulkan and Slang, with an ECS and source-generated behaviors underneath.
releaseNotes:
The dither draws its grain from a table of blue noise, on unless a program turns it off, at a strength a program sets from 0 to 1, a half the calmest grain that leaves no band.
The still glow test draws strips a few tens of pixels wide at the rows it needs, and the ceiling's test narrower windows, so a device that draws on its CPU runs each in about a minute.
The dither is off unless a program turns it on, so the window draws as before in the dark until a grain the eye does not see is in.
A glow texel looks the frame before up less its point's offset from the texel's middle, so a still view at 1,440 rows holds its blend's 32 frames where it held one and a half.
The engine packs as one package again, 3DEngine carrying every area's assembly, documentation and symbols with the Sky module's, and the pack job measures it against the size nuget.org takes before anything is kept or pushed.
The window's frame is dithered before its eight bits take it, a grain of up to a level that holds still unless temporal antialiasing blends the frames, so a slow gradient in the dark no longer falls in bands.
A glow texel's point is found at the middle of the depth's texel it takes its depth from, so a ceiling seen at a slant in a window of 1,440 rows takes the light it takes at 1,080, with no line across it.
The screen's probes and the glow texels take their points from the depth as ways from the eye, so a wall far from the origin no longer lights in stripes.
The probes' pipelines are made together on workers at the first frame that traces them, the frame waiting for all.
Vortice.Vulkan goes to 3.3.0, AssimpNetter to 6.0.5 and StbImageSharp to 2.30.16, its license named as it now declares it.
The command pipelines.wait answers once no pipeline is being made on the workers or in the driver.
The hall of glowing blocks the faint lights' test reads is small enough to settle on a device that draws on its CPU.
A client that names no session looks for one again as a named one does, and says what its first look saw of each file.
A glow light giving a probe's ray's hit under a 32nd of the largest before it is taken as one point at its box's middle.
The coarser cascades trace half their probes a frame once the lights and the field have kept still for the frames a change takes to settle.
title: 3DEngine
